title: The Akhand Kirtani Jatha
hookLine: a movement known for all-night kirtan and strict discipline

cards: It's past midnight in a hall with the lights turned low. Most of the city is asleep. On the floor, rows of people sit cross-legged, some swaying a little, some with eyes closed.
A harmonium starts a line, and the whole room sings it back. Then again. Then a new verse.
Nobody checks the time. Hours later, a gray light comes through the high windows, and the singing is still going. People call this a rainsabaee, a night that lasts the whole night.
A group known for it is today's stream.

teach.h: AKHAND KIRTANI JATHA: THE UNBROKEN SINGERS.
teach.b: Take the name apart. Akhand means unbroken. Kirtani means those who do kirtan, the singing of the Guru's hymns.

Jatha means a band, a company that moves together. So: the company of unbroken singing. Tradition traces the group to Bhai Randhir Singh, a Sikh remembered for long hours of devotion and a strict life.
Two things mark the Jatha. The first is kirtan itself. Its programs often run through the night, in a plain, congregational style.

The sangat doesn't only listen; it sings, repeating lines together until the repetition becomes a kind of breathing. Members speak of that late, shared singing as a way the Name settles into a person.
The Jatha is known for keeping the rehat strictly, and some members keep observances beyond the common code, in diet and daily practice.
Not every Sikh sees those extra observances the same way, and that question is left to the panth. What the Jatha leans on comes from the Granth.
Guru Arjan, in Raag Maru on Ang 1075, says in paraphrase that in this dark age, singing the Lord's praise is the foremost thing.

teach.h: ANG 1075: KIRTAN STANDS AT THE FRONT.
teach.b: Kirtan isn't decoration on the side of worship; in that line, it stands at the front. And why the night?
Gurbani speaks of the amrit vela, the ambrosial hours before dawn, as a time for the Name. A night of kirtan walks straight into those hours instead of waking up for them.
Few people can give a whole night to anything, but the shape still teaches: a song kept going long enough stops being a performance and becomes a place you live for a while.

how: At Akhand Kirtani Jatha programs, the sangat sings Gurbani together, often through an entire night in a rainsabaee kirtan, repeating lines after the lead singers until dawn.

games.why: a rainsabaee walks straight into the ambrosial hours. the singers arrive at dawn already singing.

practice: If you have a recording of Gurbani kirtan, put it on quietly; if not, simply listen to the room.
Let one repeated line or sound carry your breath in and out, without trying to follow every word, and if you pray, rest on Waheguru between the lines.

wordCard.voice: The Akhand Kirtani Jatha. A Sikh company known for kirtan that runs through the night, and for keeping the rehat strictly. Akhand: unbroken. Today's word.
